answer: The Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm employs a Sybil-resistance mechanism by leveraging a "willow tree" structure, where agents form a hierarchical network of "zephyr" nodes, each with a unique identifier. As a malicious agent attempts to create a fake identity, it will trigger a ripple effect, causing other agents to verify its identity with the root node, ultimately revealing the fake identity and excluding it from the network.
